Firmus newsroom (7 Aug 2026; Bloomberg, TechNode Global and Seeking Alpha the same day): full commitments for a USD$2 billion strategic equity investment round with follow-on participation from Coatue and NVIDIA, new investment from funds managed by Blackstone Tactical Opportunities and other Blackstone vehicles, and participation from Jane Street; post-money valuation above USD$10.5 billion; more than $3 billion of new equity raised in the past year; proceeds accelerate Project Southgate in Australia and Asia-Pacific expansion including the Indonesia development. Oliver Curtis, Co-Chief Executive Officer, is the executive quoted.
SiliconANGLE, 6 Apr 2026: Firmus raised $505 million co-led by Coatue and NVIDIA at a $5.5 billion valuation ahead of an anticipated ASX listing.

Kirkland & Ellis release and DCD, 9 Feb 2026: Firmus secured a US$10 billion debt financing facility led by funds managed by Blackstone Tactical Opportunities and Blackstone Credit & Insurance, supported by Coatue, to fund the next phase of Project Southgate; described as one of the largest private debt financings in Australian history; Southgate expected to scale to 1.6 GW through 2028.

Tech Wire Asia (Jun 2026), CRN Asia and Light Reading: Firmus' first Indonesian project is a 360 MW AI Factory campus in Batam, close to Singapore, with NVIDIA and DayOne, taking delivery of up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs from the first quarter of 2027 into 2028; Firmus said it expects up to US$30 billion of revenue over the agreement's first six years based on committed customer agreements. Initial Batam capacity targeted for Q1 2027.

Wilson Asset Management (AFR-sourced) and Capital Brief, mid-2026: Firmus and its advisers are working to put the offer in front of investors late in the September quarter with an ASX listing in the final quarter of 2026, once financing and customers for the Batam development are secured; the float had earlier been expected in June or July and was described by TheNextWeb as a targeted ~$2bn raise that would rank among the largest technology listings in Australian history. Nothing is confirmed; the timing has slipped once.

ABC News (2 Jul 2025; 15 Jun, 3 Jul, 25 Aug, 4 Sep 2026): the St Leonards, Launceston AI Factory (Project Southgate stage one) is designed for 36,000 NVIDIA GPUs across two stages on a 104 MW hydro contract with Aurora; Firmus has asked Hydro Tasmania for a long-term 450 MW contract for three Tasmanian sites (up to ~30% of the state's current use), with an outcome expected by the end of 2026; George Town council approved the 288 MW Bell Bay site 6-1 on 25 Aug 2026 despite community opposition.

TheNextWeb (Apr 2026): Firmus' modular, fully liquid-cooled AI Factories are built to run NVIDIA GPU clusters at high density; the company says its technology cuts energy consumption by 33% and water use by 99% (company claims, not independently verified).

Startup Daily: Firmus was founded in Sydney in 2019 by Oliver Curtis, Tim Rosenfield and Jonathan Levee, originally as a bitcoin miner, and is now Singapore-based (ABC News: Singaporean-headquartered with offices in Sydney); it pivoted to 'green AI factories'. No United States office or site was found in any source.

Drive.com.au and Sportcal (Feb 2025): Atlassian, formed in 2002 and headquartered in Sydney, became Williams' Official Title Partner, Official Technology Partner and Official Collaboration Software Partner in a long-term deal described as the largest in the team's history; the team races as Atlassian Williams Racing.
SmartCompany: Australian technology companies Atlassian (Williams), Airwallex (McLaren) and Airtasker (Racing Bulls) have all bought Formula 1 team sponsorships as a route to global brand awareness.
Atlassian Williams F1 Team, 2026: multi-year partnership with Anthropic naming Claude the team's Official Thinking Partner, working alongside Williams' engineers, strategists and operations teams.
Aston Martin Aramco, 22 May 2025: CoreWeave joins as Official AI Cloud Computing Partner in a multi-year partnership. Sponsor table: Core Scientific and TWG AI are on Cadillac F1 Team's 2026 roster.

Sponsor table: Williams — Atlassian title, VAST (data platform), Keeper (identity security), Airia, Brillio, Claude (joined 2026); no cloud, GPU or AI-compute partner. Cadillac: Core Scientific, TWG AI. Red Bull: Oracle (title). Mercedes and Alpine: Microsoft. McLaren: Google Cloud, Dell Technologies, Airwallex. Ferrari: HP, IBM. Audi: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (departed, last 12 months). Racing Bulls: Airtasker, Dynatrace, Confluent.

brief.industry_meta: AI Infrastructure · Liquid-Cooled NVIDIA AI Factories
brief.hq: Singapore (founded in Sydney, 2019); AI Factories in Tasmania
brief.ticker: Private (>$10.5B post-money; ASX listing targeted Q4 2026)
brief.deck: Firmus, the Sydney-founded builder of liquid-cooled NVIDIA AI Factories on Tasmanian hydro power, announced a fully subscribed $2B strategic equity round on 7 August at a post-money valuation above $10.5B, backed by Coatue, NVIDIA, Blackstone and Jane Street, with an ASX listing targeted for the fourth quarter.
brief.the_case_p1: The round is company-announced: $2B of equity from Coatue, NVIDIA, funds managed by Blackstone and Jane Street, taking new equity raised in the past year past $3B and the valuation from $5.5B in April to more than $10.5B. Beneath it sits a $10B debt facility led by Blackstone and Coatue, signed in February, for Project Southgate: liquid-cooled AI Factories in Tasmania, 36,000 NVIDIA GPUs at the Launceston site, and a 170,000-GPU campus in Batam, Indonesia, from the first quarter of 2027, against which Firmus reports up to $30B of committed revenue over six years.
brief.the_case_p2: The identity moment is the listing. Firmus and its advisers are working towards an ASX float in the final quarter of 2026 (Wilson Asset Management, Capital Brief), which at the reported size would rank among the largest technology listings in Australian history. A company about to sell itself to Australian institutions and retail investors needs a brand beyond data-centre engineers, and the local precedent is set: Atlassian, Airwallex and Airtasker all bought Formula 1 for that reason.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The round closed on 7 August and the float is targeted for the fourth quarter, so the listing's brand budget is being set now. The Singapore GP in October sits an hour from Batam, and the 2027 season opens with the Australian GP in Melbourne, the home market for the offer.
brief.why_team_para: Williams is the Australian car on the grid: Atlassian, founded in Sydney, became title partner in 2025 in the largest deal in the team's history, and the roster around it is data-native: VAST for the data platform, Keeper for identity, Claude as Official Thinking Partner. The sponsor table shows no cloud, GPU or AI-compute partner at Williams; CoreWeave holds that lane at Aston Martin Aramco, Core Scientific and TWG AI at Cadillac. Two Sydney companies on one car is a story the ASX will read.
brief.value_content: MODE A - operational. Williams' development outside the FIA aerodynamic-testing limits is GPU-bound: machine-learning surrogates, driver-in-loop and strategy simulation, telemetry analytics between sessions. Firmus supplies that capacity from liquid-cooled NVIDIA factories it says use 33% less energy and 99% less water, on demand and outside cost-cap capital. In return: Official AI Factory Partner designation, livery presence, Singapore and Melbourne hospitality for its investor and customer audience.
brief.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official AI Factory Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, spanning the listing and the Batam ramp. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-payable in compute. Scope: sidepod placement, naming of the team's compute environment, hospitality at the Australian and Singapore rounds, joint engineering content.
brief.decision_maker_bio: Curtis co-founded Firmus in Sydney in 2019, fronts every raise and holds a reported 19% stake. Path: Tim Rosenfield, Co-Founder and Co-CEO; Kirsty Godfrey-Billy, CFO, ex-Xero; Cameron Hanson, COO; Grant Dempsey, Chair. No chief marketing officer is listed.
brief.opening_angle_quote: “Oliver, Atlassian took Williams to market as the Australian team; you are taking Firmus to the ASX. The compute lane on that car is open and Singapore is an hour from Batam. 25 minutes before the Singapore GP to see the numbers?”
score_cells: Round announced 7 Aug; Singapore GP inside the window; float targeted Q4.
$2B equity at $10.5B+ and $10B of debt, but earmarked for capex.
B2B infrastructure; strong Australian tie; founder history to manage.

Route through co-CEO Rosenfield and Chair Dempsey; the ASX process will have handled disclosure.

brief.bottom_line: A company-announced $2B round at more than $10.5B, a $10B debt stack and an ASX listing targeted for the fourth quarter put Firmus at peak brand-investment motive; Williams offers the grid's only Australian-titled car and an open compute lane. Founder history and unresolved Tasmanian power hold the score at 72.

why_now.label: Trigger
why_now.text: On 7 August Firmus announced full commitments for a $2B strategic equity round at a post-money valuation above $10.5B, with follow-on money from Coatue and NVIDIA, new investment from funds managed by Blackstone, and participation from Jane Street. It is a company release, confirmed by Bloomberg the same day, and takes new equity raised in the past year past $3B.

why_now.label: Price doubled in four months
why_now.text: In April Firmus raised $505M at a $5.5B valuation; four months later the post-money print is above $10.5B. Behind the equity sits a $10B debt facility led by Blackstone and Coatue, signed in February, described as one of the largest private debt financings in Australian history.

why_now.label: The listing
why_now.text: Firmus and its advisers are working towards an ASX float in the final quarter of 2026, after an earlier mid-year target slipped; Wilson Asset Management reports the company wants up to $30B of committed revenue in hand when it launches. A listing of the reported size would rank among the largest technology IPOs in Australian history, and the brand spend that accompanies it is decided in the months before, not after.

why_now.label: Calendar window
why_now.text: The Singapore GP in October is an hour from the Batam campus where Firmus will take delivery of up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs from the first quarter of 2027; the 2027 season then opens with the Australian GP in Melbourne, in front of the investors the offer is aimed at. A deal agreed before Singapore can be announced there and launched in full at home.

why_team.label: The Australian car
why_team.text: Atlassian, founded in Sydney, became Williams' title partner in 2025 in the largest deal in the team's history. Firmus was founded in Sydney six years ago and is about to ask Australian investors to value it above $10B. Two Sydney technology companies on one car is a story the ASX, the AFR and the Melbourne crowd will read without explanation.

why_team.label: The open lane
why_team.text: Per the sponsor table, Williams carries Atlassian, VAST for the data platform, Keeper for identity, Airia, Brillio and Claude as Official Thinking Partner, and no cloud, GPU or AI-compute partner. Official AI Factory Partner is a clean category at a team-partner price.

why_team.label: A data-native roster
why_team.text: Williams' revival is data-led, and GPU capacity for surrogate models, simulation and analytics is consumed in the factory rather than merely shown on the car. That is what separates a technology partner from a logo, and it is what Firmus sells.

why_team.label: Precedent
why_team.text: Atlassian, Airwallex and Airtasker have each used a Formula 1 team to take an Australian technology brand global. Firmus would be the fourth, and the first whose product the team itself would run on.

value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)
value.text: Compute for the work outside the aerodynamic-testing restrictions: machine-learning surrogates, driver-in-the-loop and race-strategy simulation, telemetry and video analytics between sessions. Firmus supplies it on demand from liquid-cooled NVIDIA factories it says use 33% less energy and 99% less water than conventional builds, so the team gets capacity it could not fund inside the cost cap and a sustainability line it can defend.

value.label: Commercial lift for the team
value.text: A partner heading to a public listing brings Australian and Asian institutional investors, bankers and hyperscale customers to Singapore and Melbourne, an audience Williams' B2B partners want in the suite.

value.label: Content and ecosystem
value.text: A factory-to-pit-wall story: the compute behind the strategy models, filmed in Tasmania and Batam, with co-produced engineering content alongside the team's data partners.

value.label: What the team gives back
value.text: Official AI Factory Partner designation, sidepod or engine-cover placement, naming of the team's compute environment, hospitality at the Australian and Singapore rounds, driver and engineering access for Firmus' investor communications.

ruled_out.reason: CoreWeave, Official AI Cloud Computing Partner since May 2025, is a direct rival.
Core Scientific and TWG AI occupy the compute and AI lanes on the 2026 roster.
Oracle is title partner and the cloud incumbent.
Microsoft holds the cloud lane at both.
Google Cloud and Dell Technologies occupy cloud and hardware; Airwallex already owns the Australian-technology story there.
HP (title) and IBM cover compute hardware and cloud services.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise on the roster in the last 12 months; lane crowded.

ruled_out.reason: Open but not chosen: Airtasker gives Racing Bulls an Australian thread, but neither roster is data-native and neither carries an Australian title partner.

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Oliver Curtis, or with co-CEO Tim Rosenfield and Chair Grant Dempsey, before the Singapore GP to agree a Singapore announcement window and size an Official AI Factory Partner entry against Williams' 2027 roster ahead of the listing.

note:
# Firmus Technologies → Atlassian Williams Racing — verification log (N° 148, issued for 7 Aug 2026)

Built in-session on 6 Sep 2026 at no API cost (no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), with Claude as scanner, verifier and writer through the pipeline's injectable stages; the calendar table, sponsor table, 13-rule audit and 2-page render ran as code. The row came from a thin scan whose source was an aggregator (tryfundable.ai) and whose named person, "David Burt, CEO & Founder", does not exist in any Firmus source: the real leaders are co-CEOs Oliver Curtis and Tim Rosenfield. The row's "Series G" label is also wrong (the company calls it a strategic equity investment round) and its "hyperscaler anchor client secured" and "imminent ASX IPO" claims were not supported; neither is used.

**Sandbox limitation, stated plainly:** firmus.co, itwire.com, smartcompany.com.au, pulse2.com and theorg.com were egress-blocked. Every claim was checked against search summaries of the primary page named in the evidence. Treat VERIFIED lines as REPORTED until a person opens the link; confidence is MEDIUM.

## The trigger

Company-announced (Firmus newsroom, 7 Aug 2026; Bloomberg, TechNode Global, Seeking Alpha same day): a fully subscribed USD$2B strategic equity round, post-money above USD$10.5B, Coatue and NVIDIA follow-on, Blackstone funds new, Jane Street participating; more than $3B of new equity in the past year. Prior: $505M at $5.5B (Apr 2026, SiliconANGLE); $10B debt facility led by Blackstone and Coatue (9 Feb 2026, Kirkland & Ellis / DCD). Dealroom's "US$15.5B" and Startup Daily's "$15B" are AUD-basis numbers and are not used.

## Decision path

Oliver Curtis, Co-Founder & Co-CEO (quoted on the release; largest shareholder at 19%, reported). Tim Rosenfield, Co-Founder & Co-CEO. Kirsty Godfrey-Billy, CFO (ex-Xero). Cameron Hanson, COO. Daniel Kearney, CTO. Grant Dempsey, Chair. **No CMO or commercial lead is listed** in any source found.

**Reputational flag for the MD:** Startup Daily records that Curtis served 12 months in prison for insider trading, released 2017. It is in the brief's first risk row, and the ask offers Rosenfield / Dempsey as the alternative path.

## Leadership ties

`none found` after checking Curtis, Rosenfield, Godfrey-Billy, Hanson and Dempsey for F1 / FE / sponsorship history.

## Team fit

Judged only against `seeds/sponsors.json`: Williams has no cloud / GPU / AI-compute partner; Atlassian (Sydney) is title partner. Ruled out by name in `extended.ruled_out`. The Australian F1 precedent (Atlassian, Airwallex, Airtasker) is from SmartCompany and the sponsor table.

## Post-trigger updates (to 6 Sep 2026)

George Town council approved the 288 MW Bell Bay site 6-1 on 25 Aug 2026 amid community opposition; Hydro Tasmania will decide on the 450 MW request by end-2026 (ABC News, 4 Sep). Kalkine reports Firmus fast-tracking South Australian sites as Tasmanian plans stall. All in the second risk row.

## Not claimed

- No revenue figure: the "$30B" is committed-revenue expectation over six years, labelled as reported.
- No US presence found; the brief does not lean on US rounds.
- Deal size ($3-5M a year) is an ESTIMATE.
- Energy and water savings (33% / 99%) are company claims, said so in the copy.
